Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

emphasize verb

also emphasise, stress, highlight, underline, drive home, insist (that), emphasis

classical

Quint. 6.4.5 (Lewis & Short): firmissima quaeque memoriae jūdicis inculcāre
Cic. de Or. 1.127 (Lewis & Short): id quod trādātur vel etiam inculcētur

inculcō, inculcāre, inculcāvī, inculcātum

verb, first conjugation; aliquid alicui (or memoriae alicujus)

drive home, impress (a point) on someone

To hammer a point in by saying it again and again; Lewis & Short glosses Cic. Att. 16.3.1 “emphasized by additions”. Literally to tread or ram in, and so also to cram in where it doesn’t belong (Graeca verba inculcāre, Cic. Off. 1.111).

Other words

  • īnstō, īnstāre, īnstitī, īnstātum — insist, press (a point)

    verb, first conjugation; with an accusative and infinitive, or the dative of the person pressed · also used · classical · Ter. And. 147: ille īnstat factum; Cic. Att. 13.32.1 (Lewis & Short): urgē, īnstā, perfice

    To keep on at a claim or a task; literally to stand on, then to press hard on an enemy, and of time, to be at hand (Lewis & Short).

  • etiam atque etiam — again and again, urgently

    adverbial phrase, with a verb of asking, saying or thinking · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.66.2: etiam atque etiam tē rogō atque ōrō ut …

    How a Latin speaker underlines a request: said once, it means “I ask you most earnestly”. Latin also stresses a word by putting it first or last, or with ipse and quidem.

Examples

  • Ego illud sēdulō negāre factum; ille īnstat factum.

    I kept denying that it had happened; he insisted it had.Ter. And. 146–147

  • etiam atque etiam tē rogō atque ōrō ut eum … juvēs

    I ask and beg you again and again to help himCic. Fam. 13.66.2

See also important, repeat, request.

SourcesLewis & Short: inculco · Lewis & Short: insto · Lewis & Short: etiam

Ter. And. 146–147 and Cic. Fam. 13.66.2 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026). Neither Morgan–Owens nor Traupman gives a word for “emphasize”.
